# docs/ System — Structured Documentation

claude-kit uses a 9-layer documentation system with traceability between layers.
Each layer has a dedicated directory, ID namespace, and document template.

## Layer Architecture

```
research/ → requirements/ → architecture/ → specs/ → code → testing/ → benchmarks/
                ↑    ↓                                          ↑
        methodology/ constraints/                        operations/ (cross-cutting)
           (meta)   (quality attributes)
```

| Layer | Directory | ID Prefix | What It Contains |
|-------|-----------|-----------|-----------------|
| Research | `docs/research/` | — | Theoretical papers (no ID prefix) |
| Requirements | `docs/requirements/` | REQ-XXX | What the system must do and why |
| Architecture | `docs/architecture/decisions/` | ADR-XXX | Immutable architecture decision records |
| Specs | `docs/specs/` | SPEC-XXX | Version-scoped implementation specs |
| Testing | `docs/testing/evidence/` | TEST-XXX | Test evidence records |
| Testing | `docs/testing/regression/` | REG-XXX | Regression analysis |
| Benchmarks | `docs/benchmarks/` | BM-XXX | Methodology, baselines, results |
| Operations | `docs/operations/incidents/` | INC-XXX | Post-incident reports |
| Operations | `docs/operations/runbooks/` | RB-XXX | Operational procedures |
| Operations | `docs/operations/migration/` | MIG-XXX | Version migration guides |
| Constraints | `docs/constraints/` | QA-XXX | Quality attributes and architectural constraints |
| Methodology | `docs/methodology/` | — | Requirements derivation, evidence quality, coverage analysis (no ID prefix) |

## When to Consult

| You are about to... | Check first |
|---------------------|-------------|
| Start a new feature | `docs/requirements/` for existing REQs, `docs/specs/` for active SPECs |
| Make an architecture decision | `docs/architecture/decisions/` for prior ADRs on the same topic |
| Prepare a release | `docs/specs/` for active SPECs, `docs/testing/` for evidence gaps |
| Debug a production issue | `docs/operations/incidents/` for similar past incidents |
| Change a core subsystem | `docs/architecture/components/` for component documentation |
| Question the requirements basis | `docs/methodology/` for derivation process and evidence grading |
| Evaluate market constraints | `docs/constraints/` for compliance, regulatory, and deployment constraints |

## When to Update

| You just... | Update |
|-------------|--------|
| Implemented a requirement | Set REQ status to `active`, link to SPEC and ADR |
| Made an architecture decision | Create a new ADR (never edit accepted ADRs) |
| Completed a spec | Set SPEC status to `completed`, create TEST evidence |
| Fixed a regression | Update REG status to `fixed`, note the fix |
| Changed a requirement | Check if downstream ADRs and SPECs need updating |

## Cross-Reference Format

When referencing documents from other layers:

```
See REQ-001 (Plugin Encryption at Rest)
```

Always include the document title in parentheses. The validation script
(`scripts/validate-docs.sh`) checks that referenced IDs resolve to real files.

## ADR Immutability Rule

**Never edit an accepted ADR.** To change a decision:

1. Create a new ADR with the next sequential ID
2. Explain in its Context section why the original is being revisited
3. Update the original's status to `superseded-by ADR-YYY` (the **only** allowed edit)

## Creating New Documents

1. Open the target layer's `INDEX.md` for the document template
2. Find the next sequential ID (if `REQ-003` exists, use `REQ-004`)
3. Name the file `<ID>-<short-description>.md` (lowercase, hyphens)
4. Include a `## Traces` section with upstream and downstream links
5. Run `bash scripts/validate-docs.sh` to verify compliance

## Validation

Docs structure is validated by `scripts/validate-docs.sh` as part of the
`fast-validate` CI job. See the testing-standards rule for details.
